issues.description: Format B assumes metrics is a dict, so truthy malformed values crash ingest with AttributeError instead of producing a warning.
Malformed Format C XML is not caught, so ET.ParseError aborts the entire ingest instead of recording a malformed_row warning.
Non-finite JSON scores such as NaN are accepted as numeric and can crash SQLite insertion or store invalid score data.
Score clamping does not reject NaN or infinity, so invalid floats bypass validation.
Blank or missing run_id/model/task values are accepted as valid records, causing empty IDs or string 'None' IDs to enter the database.
Duplicate run IDs silently overwrite records for every source, not just Format B corrections, so accidental A/C duplicates can lose data without warning.
The empty-directory error path still creates or mutates the SQLite database before returning failure.
Input files are read or parsed whole without size limits, creating avoidable memory/DoS risk on large CSV, JSONL, or XML inputs.
CSV over-split recovery uses raw comma splitting, which can corrupt rows if earlier fields are valid quoted CSV containing commas.
